items.value: Relationships 1 and 2 hold: the BUR-4 emission-decline data empirically supports the LT-LEDS claim, and the short-termism of statement III contradicts the long-horizon approach implicit in statement I
items.reasoning: Statement I is factually correct — India's Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy, submitted at COP27 in 2022, is the framework document for the net-zero-by-2070 pledge. Statement II is also factually correct: the Fourth Biennial Update Report submitted in December 2024 reported roughly a 7.93 per cent fall in greenhouse gas emissions in 2020 relative to 2019. Relationship 2 is the clearest of the three: statement III insists that climate-resilient development 'necessarily depends on quick and short-term' emission cuts, which is exactly the opposite of the long-term, phased transition that a 2070 net-zero strategy is built on, so III does contradict the approach implicit in I. Relationship 3 fails on the same ground — a statement that contradicts I cannot 'together with I' establish a premise of long-term sustainability. Relationship 1 is the judgement call and is the reason this is MED: the 2020 fall is very largely a COVID-19 lockdown artefact and predates the LT-LEDS itself by two years, so a strict reader could say it supplies no empirical support for I at all. However the option set contains no '2 only', so relationship 1 must be accepted for any option to be defensible, and read loosely — declining measured emissions being evidence that the stated pathway is credible — it does support I. RUNNER-UP: A (1 only), which would win if a marker held that III merely places a different emphasis rather than contradicting I. Note that had the setter intended '2 only', the item would be defective as printed.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; gibbons are small, light apes and have nothing of the heavy gorilla build asserted in statement 3
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Hoollongapar Gibbon Sanctuary in Jorhat district, Assam, is the flagship protected area for the Western Hoolock Gibbon, which the IUCN Red List classifies as Endangered. Statement 2 is correct and is the defining locomotor trait of the family — gibbons are the specialist brachiators among apes, with elongated forelimbs and hook-like hands that let them swing hand-over-hand through the canopy. Statement 3 is false: the Western Hoolock Gibbon is a small ape weighing roughly 6 to 9 kg, and its light frame is precisely what makes brachiation possible; a gorilla-like heavy build would be incompatible with the arboreal swinging described in statement 2, so statements 2 and 3 cannot both be true.

items.value: Only statement 3 is a valid rationale — mangroves act as natural bio-shields against tidal surges and as a biomass-based livelihood base
items.reasoning: Statement 3 is the standard climate-resilience case for mangroves: their dense stilt-root systems dissipate wave and cyclone-surge energy, earning them the description 'bio-shield', while fuelwood, honey, fodder and fisheries make them a livelihood base for coastal communities. Statement 1 is wrong on two counts — mangroves do not store freshwater, and converting them to paddy is a recognised cause of mangrove loss, not a reason to protect them. Statement 2 inverts the biology: mangrove roots are salt-tolerant, excluding or excreting salt rather than being 'salt-sensitive', and clearing mangroves for aquaculture ponds is one of the largest global drivers of mangrove destruction. Both 1 and 2 describe the conversion of mangroves to other land uses, which is the opposite of a rationale for protecting them.

items.value: Only statement 3 is correct — Vizhinjam's natural deep draft and location near the east-west shipping lane let India retain trans-shipment cargo that previously went to foreign ports
items.reasoning: Vizhinjam is India's first dedicated deep-water container trans-shipment port: a natural draft of about 20 metres needing minimal dredging, sited roughly 10 nautical miles from the main east-west shipping channel, so it can handle the largest mother vessels. Its strategic point is precisely that about three-quarters of India's trans-shipment cargo had been handled at Colombo, Singapore and Salalah, and Vizhinjam is intended to retain that traffic and the associated revenue in India — exactly statement 3. Statement 1 is false in every clause: the port is built for international trans-shipment, not domestic cargo alone, and it was developed in partnership with a private developer using foreign-supplied equipment. Statement 2 is false: it is a container port, not a cruise-tourism or heritage-shipping project.

items.value: The Sutlej — it is antecedent, rises on the Tibetan Plateau, crosses China, India and Pakistan, is a major irrigation river, and being a tributary of the Indus it never builds distributaries
items.reasoning: All four clues have to be satisfied together, and clue 4 is what decides the item. The Sutlej rises near Rakas Lake close to Mansarovar on the Tibetan Plateau, cuts a deep antecedent gorge across the Himalaya, flows through China (Tibet), India and Pakistan, and feeds the Bhakra-Nangal system and the canal network of Punjab and Rajasthan; because it is a tributary that merges into the Indus through the Panjnad, it never reaches the sea and so forms no distributaries. The Indus and the Brahmaputra each satisfy the first three clues — both are classic antecedent rivers rising on the Tibetan Plateau and each crosses three countries — but both build large deltas with well-developed distributaries, so both fail clue 4. The Teesta fails clue 2, flowing through only India and Bangladesh.

items.value: Statements 2 and 3 are the incorrect ones — West Bengal, not Rajasthan, has the longest international border among States, and Meghalaya also touches only one other State
items.reasoning: The question asks which statements are NOT correct. Statement 1 is correct, so it is not part of the answer: Uttar Pradesh borders eight States — Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Bihar — more than any other State (Assam is next with seven). Statement 2 is incorrect: Rajasthan has the longest border with Pakistan, about 1,070 km, but the longest international border of any Indian State belongs to West Bengal, which shares roughly 2,217 km with Bangladesh besides its frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan. Statement 3 is incorrect: Sikkim indeed touches only West Bengal, but Meghalaya likewise touches only Assam among Indian States, so Sikkim is not the only such State.

items.value: Only statement 1 is correct — the Doyang Lake story is a community-conservation success; tracking technology does not guide the birds, and the falcons remain passage migrants
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct and is the whole significance of the Doyang episode: villages around the reservoir, notably Pangti, turned from mass trapping of the falcons in 2012 to organised protection, and Nagaland is now described as the Amur Falcon capital of the world. Statement 2 is false as worded — satellite transmitters fitted to individual falcons allow researchers to observe the migration route; they play no part in guiding the birds, whose navigation is innate. Statement 3 is false: the Amur Falcon is a passage migrant that halts at Doyang for a few weeks to fatten before the non-stop crossing of the Arabian Sea to southern Africa; there is no permanent resident population in India.

items.value: Only statement 3 is an RAD objective — raising productivity and reducing climatic risk through Integrated Farming Systems
items.reasoning: Rainfed Area Development is the component of the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture built around the Integrated Farming System, which combines crops with horticulture, livestock, fishery, apiculture and agro-forestry so that a farmer's income does not collapse when a single crop fails — exactly statement 3. Statement 1 is the opposite of the scheme's logic: RAD promotes diversification, and monoculture is precisely the vulnerability it is designed to reduce. Statement 2 is out of scope twice over, since RAD targets rainfed and not irrigated areas, and promoting more rice in irrigated regions belongs to a different policy stream altogether.

items.value: Both statements are correct — Oeko-Tex certification of Eri silk both opens high-end chemical-free markets and formally attests conformity with international standards for premium eco-conscious buyers
items.reasoning: The two statements are two faces of the same implication. Oeko-Tex certification tests textiles against a harmful-substances list, and for Assam's Eri silk it supplies the third-party attestation that European and other premium buyers demand — so statement 1 follows directly, since exporters can now bid for high-end segments that require chemical-free assurance, and statement 2 states the same result in the language of formal conformity that opens eco-conscious markets. The near-duplication of the two statements is itself a signal that both are intended to be accepted. RUNNER-UP: A (1 only). It would win if the marker read statement 2 strictly, because the Oeko-Tex Standard 100 label certifies freedom from harmful substances for human-ecological safety and does not, by itself, certify 'quality' or environmental performance — those belong to the separate STeP and Made in Green schemes. If that strictness is applied, statement 2 overreaches and only statement 1 survives.

items.value: Bahrain and Qatar — both lie inside the Persian Gulf, so their shipping must pass the Strait of Hormuz to reach the Indian Ocean
items.reasoning: The Strait of Hormuz is the only sea outlet of the Persian Gulf, connecting it through the Gulf of Oman to the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean. Bahrain is an island State within the Persian Gulf and Qatar is a peninsula projecting into it, so vessels from both must transit Hormuz. Syria has no Persian Gulf frontage at all; its ports at Latakia and Tartus are on the Mediterranean, and its shipping would reach the Indian Ocean through the Suez Canal and the Red Sea. Egypt likewise fronts the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, reaching the Indian Ocean via Bab-el-Mandeb, never through Hormuz.

items.value: Ecuador — Tungurahua is an Andean stratovolcano in central Ecuador near Banos, and its surroundings form the Tungurahua Volcano UNESCO Global Geopark
items.reasoning: Tungurahua is a well-known active stratovolcano of the Ecuadorian Andes, rising above the town of Banos de Agua Santa in Tungurahua province, and its eruptive episodes from 1999 onward are among the most closely monitored in South America. The volcano's location fixes the answer independently of the Geopark designation: the peak and the province of the same name lie wholly in Ecuador, so Peru, Bolivia and Colombia are excluded on geography alone.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — Madhav National Park became a Tiger Reserve in 2025 and contains the Ramsar-listed Sakhya Sagar, but it lies wholly within Madhya Pradesh
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: Madhav National Park in Shivpuri district was notified in March 2025 as India's 58th Tiger Reserve and Madhya Pradesh's ninth. Statement 2 is correct: Sakhya Sagar, a lake created on the Manier river in the 1920s, lies inside the park and was designated a Ramsar Site of international importance in 2022. Statement 3 is false: the park is situated entirely in Shivpuri district of Madhya Pradesh and shares no part of its area with Rajasthan.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; December to May is the islands' dry season, not the period of maximum precipitation
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct — the Andaman and Nicobar Islands have a warm, humid, tropical coastal climate with a small annual temperature range moderated by the surrounding sea. Statement 2 is correct and is the islands' distinctive feature: they receive rain from the south-west monsoon between about May and September and again from the retreating north-east monsoon between about November and December, giving them a long wet season. Statement 3 is false and in fact reverses the picture: December to May is the relatively dry part of the year on the islands, with rainfall building from May onward and peaking during the monsoon months.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 are Peninsular features; deep V-shaped valleys cut by fast-flowing rivers belong to the young Himalayan mountains, not to the Peninsular Block
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: the Peninsula has stood as a rigid block since the Cambrian, the recognised exception being part of its western coast, which is submerged beneath the sea, and other parts altered by tectonic movement and block faulting. Statement 2 is correct: the Peninsula's relief is dominated by worn-down residual mountains, the standard examples being the Aravali hills, the Nallamala hills, the Javadi hills, the Veliconda hills, the Palkonda range and the Mahendragiri hills. Statement 3 is false for the Peninsular Block: its rivers are graded, near base level and flow in broad, shallow valleys, whereas deep V-shaped valleys and gorges cut by swift, actively downcutting rivers are the signature of the youthful Himalayan region. Since statement 2 is certainly correct and statement 3 certainly incorrect, only an option pairing them without 3 can stand.

items.value: Relationships 1 and 2 hold: the growth and ranking data validate the port-led strategy, and Sagarmala 2.0 extends that strategy into a future-oriented innovation framework
items.reasoning: Statement I states the core Sagarmala aim of port-led development through cost-effective, sustainable coastal infrastructure; statement II reports outcomes — growth in coastal and inland waterway traffic and better global port rankings — which is exactly the kind of evidence that validates the strategy in I, so relationship 1 holds. Statement III describes Sagarmala 2.0 carrying the same port-led logic forward into a maritime innovation agenda tied to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047, which extends rather than displaces the objectives in I, so relationship 2 holds. Relationship 3 fails because statement I is not confined to traditional infrastructure and nothing in it is inconsistent with the modernisation described in III; an extension is not a contradiction, so relationships 2 and 3 cannot both be true.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 are correct — the Foxtail orchid is epiphytic and is the State flower of both Arunachal Pradesh and Assam, but it is not endemic to North-east India
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is certainly correct: Rhynchostylis retusa grows as an epiphyte on tree trunks and branches, drawing moisture from the air through aerial roots rather than rooting in soil. Statement 2 is certainly false: the species is distributed widely across tropical and sub-tropical Asia, from India, Sri Lanka, Nepal and Bhutan through Myanmar, Thailand and Indo-China to Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines, so it is not endemic to North-east India. Statement 3 is the pivot: Rhynchostylis retusa is the State flower of Assam, where it is the Kopou phul of Bihu songs, and it is also recorded as the State flower of Arunachal Pradesh, which makes the statement correct as printed. RUNNER-UP: A (1 only). It would win if Arunachal Pradesh's State flower is in fact some other orchid, since statement 3 claims both States and a single wrong State makes it false; this item rests on a recalled State-symbol fact rather than on anything in the stem, which is why it is not marked HIGH.

items.value: Only statement 3 — the Moidams are the burial mounds of Ahom royalty and nobility at Charaideo
items.reasoning: The Moidams of Charaideo in Assam, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2024, are the vaulted burial mounds in which the Ahom kings and nobles were interred with their possessions, a mound-burial tradition the Tai-Ahoms carried into the Brahmaputra valley and maintained for some six centuries. They served no military or recreational purpose, so statements 1, 2 and 4 — fortresses, recreation centres and battle-drill grounds — are all false, leaving statement 3 alone.

items.value: Better production, better nutrition, better environment and better life — the four aspirations of FAO's Strategic Framework, applied to Blue Transformation
items.reasoning: The 'Four Betters' are the aspirations set out in FAO's Strategic Framework 2022-31 for transforming agri-food systems: better production, better nutrition, a better environment and a better life, the last carrying the leave-no-one-behind commitment. Blue Transformation is FAO's programme for applying that same framework to aquatic food systems through sustainable aquaculture, effective fisheries management and upgraded value chains, so it inherits the four aspirations unchanged. Options A, C and D each swap one of the four for an ocean-specific item — better ocean, better coral reefs, better estuaries, better mangrove vegetation — none of which belongs to the Four Betters.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 only — Lake Turkana is the world's largest desert lake and a World Heritage Site nicknamed the Jade Sea, but it lies in Kenya and Ethiopia, not South Sudan
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: Lake Turkana is the largest permanent desert lake in the world and also the largest alkaline lake. Statement 3 is correct: the Lake Turkana National Parks, comprising Sibiloi National Park and the South and Central Island parks, are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, and the lake's algae-tinted colour has earned it the name Jade Sea. Statement 2 is false on both counts — the lake lies in the Great Rift Valley of northern Kenya with its northern tip extending into Ethiopia, not in South Sudan, and it is nowhere near the Sahara, whose eastern fringe is far to the north.

items.value: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project in Meghalaya
items.reasoning: The Khasi Hills Community REDD+ project, run in the Umiam-Mawphlang watershed of Meghalaya by a federation of ten indigenous Khasi kingdoms, was India's first community-owned REDD+ project and the first in the country validated and certified under the Plan Vivo standard. It protects and regenerates dense sacred and community forests while channelling carbon revenue back to the participating villages. The Uttarakhand, ICFRE-ICIMOD transboundary and Sikkim Mamley Kamrang initiatives are later or differently framed projects and none of them holds the first Plan Vivo certification in India.
